producer_report.summary: Added docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-1.md: verdict approve with changes (0 blockers, 7 major, 8 minor, 2 nits). It answers the design's eight §9 checks in order. Each finding cites a design section or a BRIEF.md line. It has a decisions-for-the-user list and a read/experiments appendix (S1–S5), and makes no firstmate claims. The main majors are: a waiver can bypass the evidence rules; citation and pin holes; four §5.4 rules that need judgment; the model can't express multi-agent or fan-out cases; the run step has no containment although v0 §16.2 said the first job running third-party code would need it; no redaction and no spend metering for the studied system; and the run record lacks BRIEF:298-299 visibility. I updated the design's status line to link review 1 and added a CHANGELOG entry. fmt, clippy and the xtask policy tests passed after my edits. The full workspace test passed before the edits, and I did not rerun it afterwards.

checks_run.note: 8 policy tests passed, including non-rust-files, architecture, enforcement-map and the boundary scanner over docs. I did not rerun the whole workspace after the doc edits, since only markdown changed.

open_issues: The brief's deliverables list names docs/non-rust-files.md and docs/decisions.md, but acceptance criterion 5 allows only the review, the design and CHANGELOG. I followed the criterion and left both unchanged. The non-rust-files check passes because *.md is already listed, and decision-log entries wait for the user's answers.
Check 8 (only the design was added) cannot be fully verified from a one-commit snapshot. The review says so and relies on a repository search plus the design's own statement.
The review's findings are unanswered and need the user's decisions (eight listed in the review).
mistakes: My first draft of finding M4 contained a stray note ('BRIEF.md:323 is not needed'). I caught it on re-read and fixed it.
learnings: The baseline passes cargo test unchanged. I never saw the earlier rejection's cause, so it may have been a boundary-scanner term in the first attempt's markdown.
xtask policy tests scan docs for banned boundary words and paths (xtask/tests/policy.rs). docs/non-rust-files.md already lists *.md, so a new review file needs no inventory change.
Athena's [budget] caps in athena.toml meter only Athena's own reader, producer and verifier roles and the job, not a studied system's own model calls.
athena-v0.md §16.2 says containment is pulled in by the first job that runs code not written by Athena's agents. The study design's run step is that job.
All BRIEF.md line citations in the design are accurate at this commit.
desires: The text of the rejected earlier job's check failure, to confirm its cause rather than infer it.
